# Showdown and side pots, explained simply

*Who shows first, why “cards speak”, and a step-by-step way to split the pot when players are all-in for different amounts.*

3 min read · Updated 2026-09-26

## Who shows first

- If there was a bet or raise on the river, the **last player to bet or raise** shows first.
- If everyone checked the river, the **first player left of the button** shows first, then clockwise.
- Once a winning hand is shown, the others can **muck** (throw away face down) instead of showing a losing hand.
- When a player is all-in and no more betting is possible, everyone still in turns their cards face up straight away, then the rest of the board is dealt — standard in tournaments; agree whether your cash game does the same.

## Cards speak

What you hold is what counts, not what you say. If someone calls “two pair” but actually has a straight, they have a straight. That’s why the golden rule at showdown is: **turn both cards face up on the table** and let the dealer read the hand. Don’t muck a hand until the pot has been pushed — a hand thrown into the discards is dead.

## Why side pots exist

You can only win from each opponent as much as you put in yourself. When a player goes all-in with fewer chips than the others, the extra chips the others keep betting go into a separate **side pot** that the all-in player can’t win.

## Worked example

Three players get their chips in on the flop. **Ana** has 100 chips, **Ben** has 300, **Cara** has 500. Ana goes all-in for 100, Ben goes all-in for 300, Cara calls 300 and keeps 200 back.

1. Line up the all-in amounts from smallest to largest: 100 (Ana), 300 (Ben).
2. **Main pot:** each player puts in up to the smallest all-in, 100 × 3 players = **300**. Ana, Ben and Cara can all win it.
3. **Side pot:** the next layer, from 100 up to 300, is 200 × 2 players = **400**. Only Ben and Cara can win it.
4. Anything above the largest all-in that nobody else matched (none here) goes back to its owner.

| Pot | Amount | Who can win it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Main pot | 300 | Ana, Ben, Cara |
| Side pot | 400 | Ben, Cara |

At showdown, Ana has the best hand, Ben the second best. Ana wins the **main pot (300)**. The side pot goes to the better hand **between Ben and Cara**, so Ben wins **400**. Ana ends with 300, Ben with 400, Cara with the 200 she kept back.

> **Tip — Award the pots from last to first:** Settle the newest side pot first, then work back to the main pot. It keeps chips from getting mixed up.

## Split pots and odd chips

When hands tie, split the pot evenly. If a chip can’t be divided, the common rule gives the **odd chip** to the first tied player left of the button. With several side pots, split each one separately.
